intended_object: The coefficient functor of degree −1 Tate cohomology of a profinite group G with level-compact coefficients: A ↦ Ĥ⁻¹(G,A) := lim over open normal S of Ĥ⁻¹(G/S, A^S), taken along the deflation maps, as a compact Hausdorff abelian group. Ĥ⁻¹(G/S, A^S) is the kernel of the norm from (A^S)_{G/S} to A^G. Inferred from the docstring, the module docs and the `_obj` lemma identifying it with `compactNegativeOneTateLimit`.
explanation: The body composes `compactFiniteNegativeOneDeflationDiagramFunctor` with `lim`. That functor sends A to the diagram S ↦ finiteTateNegOne A L S, the compact kernel of the norm from (A^S)_{G/S} to A^G, i.e. Ĥ⁻¹(G/S, A^S). Its transition maps for S ≤ T are the kernel maps induced by coinvariant deflation (deflation in degree −1). On a morphism f it gives the stagewise kernel maps, with naturality and functoriality proved. Taking `lim` gives exactly `compactNegativeOneTateLimit A.rep A.levelCompact`, proved by rfl in `compactNegativeOneTateLimitFunctor_obj`, together with the induced limit maps. This matches the standard definition of exceptional-degree Tate cohomology of a profinite group as a projective limit along deflation, here with compact coefficients so the limit lives in CompHaus abelian groups. The compactness data and the single universe u are what make each stage compact Hausdorff and let the limit over `OpenNormalSubgroup G : Type u` exist. The ring R is any commutative ring. Mathlib has no profinite Tate cohomology, so there is no counterpart.
